content:
maria: quick follow-up on the locality-aware async-evictor RFC — want a short sync. TL;DR: canary showed better avg throughput but worse p95 latency for small batches when locality scoring is enabled. thinking we missed a boundary between placement windows and eviction stalls.

dan: saw the same in the canary logs. p95 spikes around 120ms -> 260ms after a burst of mixed-tenant workloads. spike aligns with `pending_evictions` backlog.

charlie: I have a hypothesis: locality_window_ms is keeping pages pinned on the local staging pool too long which blocks fast hot-path allocations. eviction becomes async but still contends on the staging mutex.

liz: can we confirm with the resident->pending transition telemetry? I sketched a metric set: `resident_count`, `pending_evictions`, `evict_duration_ms`, `locality_score_hist` — that should show the regime where locality helps vs hurts.

maria: good. I pulled a short trace from canary host (snippet):

[2026-03-18T14:02:12Z] alloc(tensor=3.2MB) -> host-staging hit
[2026-03-18T14:02:12Z] locality_score=0.82 -> prefer local reuse
[2026-03-18T14:02:12Z] pending_evictions=72
[2026-03-18T14:02:12Z] evict_start
[2026-03-18T14:02:12Z] allocation_blocked(18ms) -> p95 bump

charlie: that matches. two quick ideas: (A) make locality_window adaptive to pending_evictions, or (B) split the fast path: if pending_evictions > threshold, bypass locality and allocate from remote staging immediately.

dan: +1 for split fast path. Adaptive windows add complexity (tuning hysteresis). Bypass looks simple: add `evict_backpressure_threshold`. pseudocode:

if pending_evictions > evict_backpressure_threshold:
  use_remote_staging()
else:
  attempt_local_reuse(locality_window_ms)

liz: add metric `bypasses_due_to_backpressure` so we can see how often policy triggers. also want a small A/B: run bypass on 20% of requests first.

maria: agreed. also worried about fragmentation: bypassing local reuse may increase remote churn and worsen cross-node transfer. need to instrument `remote_write_io_bytes` and `avg_remote_eviction_size`.

charlie: right. we should cap bypass to small allocations (<8MB) initially. Those are latency-sensitive and cheaper to remote-copy.

offload-bot: deploy started: canary/evict-bypass-experiment v3 -> 6 hosts. config

evictor:
  mode: async
  locality_window_ms: 50
  evict_backpressure_threshold: 64
  bypass_small_allocations_lt_bytes: 8388608
  max_pending_evictions: 128
  metrics: [evict_duration_ms, pending_evictions, bypasses_due_to_backpressure]

maria: experiment plan: 2d canary, collect p50/p95/p99, remote_io bytes, fragmentation delta. rollout steps:
- day0: enable 20% bypass sampling + metrics (charlie)
- day1: if p95 improves and remote_io < 1.2x baseline -> expand to 100% for small allocs (dan)
- day2: if fragmentation rises > 5% -> revert and try adaptive window idea (liz)

charlie: I'll own the sampling rollout and add `evict_backpressure_threshold` gating in the allocator. PR incoming — will also add the `bypass_reason` enum for observability.

dan: I'll add dashboards: heatmap of p95 vs pending_evictions and a time-series for `bypasses_due_to_backpressure`.

liz: I'll collect baseline fragmentation today and wire `remote_write_io_bytes` in the offload exporter.

maria: final ask: we should also spec an API change for the allocator boundary — small patch: expose `Allocator::try_allocate_with_locality(limit_ms)` that returns `LocalReuse|RemoteAlloc|Blocked`. that'll let upper layers decide to block or fallback. keep the API minimal.

charlie: that API looks good. I'll put it in the RFC follow-up doc and include a short compatibility shim for older callers.

maria: ok team — action owners: charlie (impl + PR), dan (dashboards), liz (metrics baseline), maria (rollout coord). checkin tomorrow EOD. :thumbsup:

dan: noted. starting dashboard now.

charlie: PR draft up in ~2h. linking afterwards.

offload-bot: canary telemetry: initial 6h snapshot -> p95 small-allocation latency reduced by 15% on bypass-sampled requests; overall p95 across host unchanged (+3%). more data needed.

maria: thanks — we'll reconvene after 24h. if anyone uncovers regression patterns tag #release-war-room and ping me.

liz: one more thought — add a per-tenant soft-residency budget so noisy tenants can't hold locality hints forever. follow-up if we see tenant-level hotspots.

maria: good call. adding to the follow-up backlog.

(End of thread)
